Through experimentation, practice, and maybe some help from a teacher, you have learned new forms of battle. Fighting Stances are methods of combat that grant the user pros and cons, but only while in use.

You know 2 Fighting Stances, listed below. So long as you meet a known stance’s requirements, you can enter a Fighting Stance before taking an action on your first turn in combat, after an attack action, or as a minor action.

You automatically exit and are unable to enter Fighting Stances while you do not meet the stance’s requirements, are @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.RK3DF56CKMQUV6DM]{Prone}, @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.PEDR1J13VZXKUF3C]{Stunned}, or @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.9KB959MRZ0H4IT4C]{Unconscious}, or sheathe, drop, or lose possession of your weapon. If you exit a stance instead of swapping to another, you retain the stance’s Cons until the start of your next turn.
If a stance requires a weapon trait, all wielded weapons (except shields and natural weapons) must share that trait. Shields and natural weapons, however, do not gain the stance’s pros.


Learning New Stances: You learn 2 more stances at each Growth Level.
Many Fighter Sub-Classes have expanded Fighting Stance options. Once the unlock requirements for Fighting Stances from that Sub-Class have been met, you are able to choose Fighting Stances from that list when learning new stances as part of level up.
